clue.text: Notice a port with nothing leaving on time

indicators.note: leaving says the nothing-letter departs from the port's name

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel ferry port in Kent
nothing is zero, a round letter O

explanation.surface: A news item about a harbour falling silent, with nothing leaving on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' here is a noun, a public announcement, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice and an advertisement are both public announcements, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Atheist — he is going out, wanting a church to join!

indicators.note: going out says the letters of he is leave the word atheist

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An atheist leaves, not wanting to join a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' removes H, E, I, S from ATHEIST, leaving ATT; then A and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach is to fasten or connect things together, which is to join them.

clue.text: 'Bit of a brain'? Possibly isn't clever, not first in school

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters that remain may be rearranged
not says the school's opening letter is excluded from the fodder

parts.note: the letters of isn't clever, apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of the word school

explanation.surface: A teasing query whether a brain part might be dim, not top of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first in school' removes S from ISNTCLEVER; 'Possibly' rearranges INTCLEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is one of the fluid-filled cavities within the brain, so it is part of that organ.

clue.text: Analysis of something in poor shape

definitions.meaning: a summary or detailed review of something

explanation.definitionFit: A rundown is a point-by-point summary, while run-down describes something shabby or worn out.

clue.text: A social event about five — daughter got on

indicators.note: about means the gathering's word goes round the numeral

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone reports a party at five o'clock where their daughter got on well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside DANCE (DVANCE), after A and before D.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to progress or make headway, the same as getting on in life.

clue.text: Midlands town with flighty Romeo who made many laugh?

parts.note: Dudley is a town in the West Midlands of England

indicators.note: flighty suggests the letters of Romeo are fickle and change places

explanation.surface: A tale of a fickle Romeo from a Midlands town who was a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' rearranges ROMEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudley Moore was an English comedian and actor, so he was someone who amused audiences.

clue.text: Lover of a doctor admitting sticky situation

indicators.note: admitting says the doctor lets the sticky situation inside

parts.note: a mire is a bog, or a messy predicament

explanation.surface: A doctor's lover owning up to an awkward predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone who adores or courts another person, a lover in the older sense.

clue.text: Minister in study digesting article

indicators.note: digesting means the study word swallows the article

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A clergyman reading and taking in an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a government post; here it is a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral, so a minister of religion.

clue.text: Badly pressed, I vanish into thin air maybe

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of pressed and I are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone, poorly ironed, wishes to disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges PRESSED and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter and dissipate, and vanishing into thin air is one way to do so.

clue.text: Number of important building — worker is one renting

parts.note: Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence
a worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A worker in an important building turns out to be just a renter there.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 Downing Street is the UK Prime Minister's official home, so its number is TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a person who rents property from a landlord.

clue.text: Do mend broken front and back of this — bits and bobs needed

indicators.note: broken says the letters of do mend are smashed and reassembled
front and back of picks the first and last letters of the word this

explanation.surface: An instruction to repair something broken, with odds and ends needed for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns DOMEND into ODDMEN; 'front and back of' this gives TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover scraps and miscellaneous small items, just like bits and bobs.

clue.text: Vehicle has all but come into contact with ornamental panel

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: all but means every letter except the last one is kept

parts.note: having come into contact with something is having touched it

explanation.surface: A car has almost hit a decorative panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... come into contact with' gives TOUCHED; 'all but' drops its final D.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is a carved or painted decorative frame or tablet, often scroll-shaped, used in architecture.

clue.text: Visit to tell someone at shop what is wanted — it's open for business

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit
taken as written

parts.words: tell someone at shop what is wanted
parts.note: to order is to ask a shopkeeper for goods

explanation.surface: A shopper visiting a store to request goods, as the shop opens.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'business' means a meeting's agenda, not trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairperson calls a meeting to order to formally start its proceedings, opening it for business.

clue.text: Some underwear in separate wash

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to wash some underwear separately from the rest of the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with clean water, a close synonym of washing.

clue.text: Coral and gemstone possibly seen as types of rock

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of coral and gemstone may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Coral and a gemstone being classed as kinds of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CORAL and GEMSTONE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Conglomerates are sedimentary rocks made of rounded pebbles cemented together, so they are kinds of rock.

clue.text: Army ascending by narrow hilltop — many died in disaster here

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force

indicators.note: ascending in a down clue means the word by is read upwards

parts.note: a ridge is a long narrow hilltop

explanation.surface: Troops climbing a narrow ridge to a site of tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascending' turns BY to YB. The Tay Bridge in Scotland collapsed under a train in 1879, killing everyone aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1879 collapse of this Scottish rail crossing was a disaster in which many perished.

clue.text: Europeans leaning forward endlessly to get answer

indicators.note: endlessly says the slanting word loses its last letter

parts.note: italic type slants forwards

explanation.surface: Europeans leaning in endlessly to get an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the C from ITALIC.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Italy are inhabitants of a European country, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: What superior insurance company may have is honesty

definitions.text: What superior insurance company may have
definitions.meaning: a top insurer might offer the finest cover contract
the proverb says honesty is the finest course to follow

explanation.surface: A musing that a top insurer's best product is honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue completes the proverb 'Honesty is the best policy'; 'policy' also means an insurance contract.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an insurer's finest contract and the course the proverb says honesty is.

clue.text: Consumed by fear, the deer's gone to ground

indicators.note: consumed by says the letters are swallowed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A frightened deer has hidden itself away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of deer's stands for 'has': the deer has gone to ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that has earthed has hidden in a burrow, which is going to ground.

clue.text: International receivers of news crying

parts.note: ears receive heard news

explanation.surface: Foreign listeners weeping over the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in tears means weeping, the same state as crying.

clue.text: It sounds like material was wobbly

indicators.note: it sounds like says a word for a material is spoken to give the entry

parts.note: suede is a soft leather material

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a fabric seemed unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that swayed moved unsteadily from side to side, so it wobbled.

clue.text: Animal having drink by English lake rolled over

indicators.note: rolled over says the string of drink, English and lake is turned round

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An animal with a drink beside an English lake topples over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled over' reverses RUMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a primate found in Madagascar, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Help them briefly set up channels of communication

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: aid means help
'em is a clipped form of them

explanation.surface: An instruction to help some people organise broadcasting outlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses AIDEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the press, television and radio, the means by which news is communicated.

clue.text: Illegal delivery at the end of bowler's sequence may be reason for extra run

definitions.text: may be reason for extra run

indicators.note: at the end of places the illegal delivery after the bowler's sequence

parts.note: in cricket an over is the sequence of six balls a bowler sends down
in cricket a throw, rather than a straight-armed bowl, is an illegal delivery

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: an illegal ball at the end of an over leads to an extra run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an overthrow is a fielder's return that misses the stumps and lets batters run again.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild return by a fielder in cricket allows the batters additional runs, so it can cause an extra run.

clue.text: This chemical could be deadly, eh?

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of deadly and eh might form something else

explanation.surface: A wary aside that a chemical might be lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges DEADLY and EH together.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldehyde is an organic compound such as formaldehyde, an example of a chemical.

clue.text: Novelist and poet would drink litre only with great difficulty

indicators.note: would drink means the writer takes the litre inside him

parts.note: Thomas Hardy wrote both novels and poems

explanation.surface: A writer could only manage a litre with great effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would drink' puts L inside HARDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something barely, scarcely managing it, is doing it only with great difficulty.

clue.text: Aspersions from one coming down to go aboard ship

indicators.note: to go aboard says the descending craft sits inside the ship

parts.note: SS is steamship, the usual ship abbreviation
a lander is a craft that descends onto a surface

explanation.surface: Insults hurled by someone descending to board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanders are false damaging remarks, the same as aspersions cast on someone.

clue.text: A post in which one may see Conservative rise

indicators.note: in which one may see says the Conservative is found inside the post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: A job where a Tory's rise to power can be watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which one may see' puts C inside SEND, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb or go up, a synonym of rise.
